events.continuity_hook: Continues the Denver conference episode after registration opens and the setup and teardown responsibilities begin to firm up.
events.interaction_goal: Narrow the flight timing and hotel choice while keeping the Wednesday return flexible until teardown staffing is confirmed.
events.scenario_brief: Jonah revisits the Denver conference plan after the customer dinner looks unlikely but the Sunday booth setup time becomes firmer. He now needs to arrive early enough Sunday to check in, drop bags, and get to the convention center before setup starts. The official hotel block still has rooms but with stricter cancellation terms, while a nearby better-rated hotel is slightly farther from the hall and easier to cancel. The Wednesday return is still unresolved because the colleague has not confirmed whether he can handle the final teardown window.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Denver conference plan from comparison to booking once the teardown question is settled.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the conference flight and hotel booking, capture room and seating details, and prepare a concise itinerary for his calendar.
events.scenario_brief: The Denver colleague confirms he can cover the late Wednesday booth teardown, so Jonah can book a Wednesday late-afternoon return instead of staying another night. The chosen plan is a Sunday early-afternoon Bay Area departure into Denver, a well-rated hotel within a short walk of the convention center rather than the stricter official block, and a return that gives enough time for final meetings before heading to the airport. He wants the hotel confirmation checked for cancellation timing, room basics, and restaurant options nearby.

events.continuity_hook: Adds a practical pre-trip check to the Denver conference episode after the booth shipment timing changes.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm package handling, bag drop, and seat details without reopening the full conference itinerary.
events.scenario_brief: A week before the Denver conference, the booth sample shipment is delayed and may arrive at the hotel instead of the convention center. Jonah needs a quick check on whether the hotel accepts packages, whether there is a holding fee, and whether he can leave bags before check-in if the Sunday flight arrives before the room is ready. The flight plan itself is unchanged, but he also wants to verify the seat assignment while he is looking at the reservation.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new distributor and client-site episode after the Denver conference logistics are settled.
events.interaction_goal: Build a practical flight-and-hotel shortlist that protects the Wednesday site start while leaving room for a possible Thursday follow-up.
events.scenario_brief: A distributor asks Jonah to join a two-day training and site visit at a food-processing facility west of Boise. The main plant walkthrough is Wednesday morning, with a distributor prep dinner Tuesday evening and a possible Thursday morning follow-up if the plant manager wants pricing detail. Jonah wants to compare Bay Area flights into Boise that keep the Tuesday arrival reliable without creating a long layover, and he needs a hotel around Boise, Meridian, or Nampa that keeps the morning drive reasonable, has strong guest feedback, parking, and easy dinner options.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Boise-area episode after Tuesday arrival timing becomes more important than the initial broad flight search.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the safer outbound routing, settle the Meridian versus Nampa hotel trade-off, and decide whether to book a Wednesday night or hold for the possible Thursday follow-up.
events.scenario_brief: The Boise-area distributor confirms Jonah needs to inspect the demo case late Tuesday afternoon before the prep dinner, which makes the latest outbound options too tight. He now wants to compare an earlier SFO itinerary with one short connection against an Oakland option that arrives at a similar time but has less schedule cushion if the first leg slips. The hotel choice has narrowed to a Meridian property with better ratings and dining nearby versus a Nampa property closer to the plant but with fewer evening options.

events.continuity_hook: Completes the Boise-area planning thread once the Thursday in-person follow-up is dropped and the two-night plan is approved.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the flights, hotel, room notes, seat request, and a short trip summary for the distributor contact.
events.scenario_brief: The plant manager decides the pricing follow-up can happen remotely, so Jonah only needs two nights for the Boise-area trip. The selected plan is a Tuesday early-afternoon Bay Area departure with one comfortable connection into Boise, a Thursday return after the Wednesday site work and distributor debrief, and the well-rated Meridian hotel because it keeps the plant drive acceptable while offering better restaurant access. He wants the room notes to request a coffee maker and mini-fridge, and he wants a window seat if one is available at booking.
